articles.title: You can borrow and resell Nintendo’s Switch 2 game-key cards
articles.summary: Nintendo explains that unlike download codes, the game key-cards aren’t one-time use and can be used on other Switch 2 consoles like regular game carts.
articles.body: Following the reveal of Nintendo’s new game-key cards during its Nintendo Switch 2 event last week, we’re finally getting more details about why they exist and how they can be used. Although they don’t contain a physical copy of a game, Nintendo’s Tetsuya Sasaki explained to GameSpot that game-key cards aren’t permanently tied to a specific Nintendo account. The games can be inserted and played on any Switch 2 console, allowing them to be borrowed, rented, and even resold. “So key cards will start up on the console or system that it is slotted into, so it’s not tied to an account or anything,” said Sasaki. That behavior is different from the Switch games that Nintendo currently sells in retail locations, which feature a download code instead of a physical cartridge. Those codes can only be used a single time and are connected to a specific Nintendo account, preventing them from being resold at a later date. Game-key cards automatically trigger a game download when inserted into a Switch 2 console. Once the game is downloaded and installed, an internet connection “...is only required when you launch the game for the first time,” according to a support page on Nintendo’s website. After that initial launch check the game can be played without an internet connection, as long as the game-key cartridge is still inserted into the console. The game-key cards are an unusual format that merges digital game downloads and physical cartridges without quite solving the downsides of either format. Internet access is still required to download the games, and you still need the cartridges to play them. But as Nintendo of America president Doug Bowser explained to The Verge, the game-key cards primarily benefit publishers, allowing them to sell physical copies of games at retail locations that may exceed the 64GB capacity of regular Switch 2 game cartridges.

articles.title: Sony is killing discs — and showing us why it’s a terrible idea
articles.summary: Sony announced that it will stop making discs for the PS5 and is also closing the PS3 and Vita stores, which is a big blow for gaming preservation.
articles.body: The future of video game preservation just took a major hit. This morning, Sony announced that, starting in January 2028, the company will no longer produce physical PlayStation discs, which means that from that moment on you can only purchase new PS5 games digitally. At the same time, Sony also announced that it’s going to start winding down the digital stores for both the PS3 and PS Vita, helpfully illustrating one of the most pertinent issues with a digital-only future for gaming: Once the stores are gone, so are the games. It’s a terrible blow for preservation of the medium. In a lot of ways, both announcements seemed inevitable. It’s clear that consumers have largely — though not entirely — shifted to buying games digitally. According to Sony’s most recent financial results from May, around 80 percent of PS5 games sold are digital. Meanwhile, just last week, Grand Theft Auto VI developer Rockstar Games announced that when the next GTA shows up in retail stores in November, it will actually just be a code in a box, with no disc. Digital games are in some ways more convenient for players. You can prep downloads in advance, keep a big library of games on a single console, and take advantage of frequent sales. There are also some notable immediate drawbacks, like the inability to sell used games or simply share a copy with a friend. From the publisher’s perspective, digital games are more lucrative for Sony and its contemporaries, who no longer have to deal with the costs of producing discs. But a more hidden cost to the digital shift comes in the form of preserving video games. Given the complex nature of consoles and constantly changing formats, preservation is already a massive challenge. Back in 2023, the Video Game History Foundation claimed that 87 percent of classic games — defined as anything released before 2010 — were “critically endangered.” The reason for the 2010 cutoff? That’s when digital storefronts became prominent, portending an even bigger issue in the future. “Our experiences gathering data for this study suggest that these problems will intensify over time due to a low diversity of reissue sources and the long-term volatility of digital game storefronts,” the report read. [Media: The closure of digital stores isn’t new, of course; just two years ago, Nintendo shut down the storefronts for both the Wii U and the Nintendo 3DS. And while you can still (for now) download games you’ve already purchased, these closures mean that titles that are exclusive to that particular store are essentially inaccessible to everybody else. If you buy a 3DS right now, you have no way to play the classic puzzler BoxBoy. In the past, this has perhaps seemed like a minor issue, as the number of digital-exclusive games for platforms like the Wii U and PS Vita was relatively small. But with the entire medium moving toward digital, including industry-shaking giants like GTA VI, this problem becomes much more clear. Starting in 2028, every PlayStation game comes with an expiry date; as soon as the PS5’s digital store shuts down, a huge swath of games will simply become inaccessible. That means not just small digital games, but also major blockbusters. There have been some steps made to alleviate these issues. Most modern game consoles now let you carry your digital library across devices — Xbox has made some notable efforts on this front — and on PC the storefront GOG has an entire program dedicated to keeping old games playable on modern hardware. These are great and necessary efforts, but they aren’t enough on their own. For one thing, plenty still slips through the cracks; mobile games, for instance, are massively popular, but are rarely subject to preservation efforts outside of fan projects. Just as important is the fact that these efforts rely on the goodwill of platform holders. Once they shut down a store, or stop putting efforts into keeping games playable across multiple generations of hardware, the games are once again impossible to legally play. (This isn’t just a gaming problem, by the way; the shift to streaming is having a similar impact on film.) Physical media isn’t a perfect solution to these problems. Discs and cartridges will degrade over time, and they usually require specialized hardware to even use. But they at least give players and preservationists a greater degree of control over how they’re able to collect, share, and preserve these experiences, without having to deal with the whims of console makers like Sony. It’s already a nightmare trying to keep old games alive — in 2028, the problem is only going to get worse.

articles.title: How to Play the Kingdom Hearts Games in Order
articles.summary: There are 13 games in the Kingdom Hearts timeline.
articles.body:
Square Enix and Disney announced Kingdom Hearts 4 at the Kingdom Hearts 20th Anniversary event in 2022, giving us a fresh new look at Sora and what he’s been up to after he left his friends for a solo adventure at the end of Kingdom Hearts 3. To no one’s surprise, there haven’t been many updates for the sequel since then, but its recent appearance at a Nintendo Direct affirmed the game's continued development.

While we wait for more updates and a potential release date for Kingdom Hearts 4 , we’re giving you a list of Kingdom Hearts games to play in chronological order. As convoluted as the series’ plot may be, this list should give you a clear perspective on the history of the Kingdom Hearts world, how Sora was set up to be the Keyblade’s chosen one, and how Master Xehanort keeps trying to plunge the world into darkness, hence the name of the series’ first arc: the Dark Seeker Saga.

How Many Kingdom Hearts Games Are There?

The Kingdom Hearts series includes 13 games across multiple platforms, including the PSP and Game Boy Advance. Kingdom Hearts IV will be, as you can probably guess, the fourth mainline game in the series.

What Kingdom Hearts Game Should I Play First?

If you are new to the Kingdom Hearts series, we highly recommend starting off with Kingdom Hearts 2. When you play as Roxas in the beginning of the game, you get flashbacks of the most important scenes from Kingdom Hearts and Kingdom Hearts: Chain of Memories to get you up to speed on the story of the series thus far, and give insight on how Sora and Roxas are connected in the first place.

The gameplay in Kingdom Hearts 2 is also more straightforward than Kingdom Hearts, and you don’t have to play through every Gummi Ship mission more than once even when you revisit worlds. Thank us later.

How to Play Kingdom Hearts Games in Chronological Order

Kingdom Hearts χ / Unchained χ / Union χ

Apologies for grouping all the titles in one section, but Kingdom Hearts χ [chi], initially a Japan-exclusive title for PC, had been subsequently rebranded into Unchained χ and Union χ [Cross] for mobile users worldwide during the eight years it was running online. The χ refers to the χ-blade, a coveted weapon designed by two Keyblades in an “X” shape capable of unlocking Kingdom Hearts.

Kingdom Hearts Union χ is set hundreds of years before the series' events, in an era leading up to the Keyblade War. You control a newly minted Keyblade wielder in the 2D world of Daybreak Town who joins one of five factions and works to ensure its supremacy over the other four as they fight over the finite light available to the world. Union χ occurs shortly after Unchained χ, but in an alternate data world where the player relives the past to forget the Keyblade War. The game shut down in May 2021, but you can still watch cutscenes of it online. If gacha games are not your style, you can watch HD cutscenes of the events in the cinematic Kingdom Hearts χ Back Cover, which is included in Kingdom Hearts HD 2.8 Final Chapter Prologue.

As the title suggests, Kingdom Hearts Dark Road is the origin story of villain Master Xehanort set 70 years before the events of Birth by Sleep. As a young man, Xehanort is taken from Destiny Islands to Scala ad Caelum to train alongside Master Eraqus to become a Keyblade wielder and is tasked by Master Odin to search for the Lost Masters, triggering a chain of events that leads him to become the Seeker of Darkness.

Dark Road employed the same 2D graphics present in Kingdom Hearts χ and its subsequent rebranded titles, which aren’t very impressive, but the game still contained details integral to the entire series. You may not be able to play the game, but you can still watch cutscenes on YouTube to get the full scope.

Set 10 years before the events of Kingdom Hearts, Birth by Sleep is told from the vantage points of Ventus, Terra, and Aqua — all Keyblade Apprentices of Master Eraqus living in the Land of Departure. Shortly after Aqua and Terra finish their Mark of Mastery exam, with the former passing and obtaining the title of Keyblade Master and the latter failing for not keeping his darkness in check, the trio go on separate journeys to find Master Xehanort, who disappeared without a trace, and defeat the Unversed, creatures created by Xehanort’s apprentice Vanitas to attack other worlds.

Birth by Sleep dives into the origin of Sora and Master Xehanort, as Ventus had part of his heart patched up by a piece of Sora’s heart. Xehanort, meanwhile, created Vanitas from the darkness he purged from Ventus’ heart, which Xehanort deemed too frail for him to use as a vessel to forge the χ-blade, forcing him to go after Terra instead. It also explores how Sora and Riku could wield the Keyblade in the first place, as Terra bestowed the power of the Keyblade to Riku, while Aqua sensed strong ties with Sora and Riku to Ventus and Terra, respectively.

Kingdom Hearts 0.2: Birth by Sleep — A Fragmentary Passage

Although it’s safe to place A Fragmentary Passage (included in Kingdom Hearts HD 2.8 Final Chapter Prologue ) before the first Kingdom Hearts game, it acts as an epilogue to Birth by Sleep and a prologue to Kingdom Hearts 3. However, the story for this game begins shortly after the events of Dream Drop Distance because King Mickey tells the story of how he came across Aqua in the Realm of Darkness to Riku, Kairi, and Master Yen Sid.

After sacrificing herself to save Terra from the Realm of Darkness at the end of Birth by Sleep, Aqua has been wandering in darkness for 10 years, trying to find a way back to the Realm of Light. She visits the dark versions of Castle of Dreams, Dwarf Woodlands, and Enchanted Dominion to battle hordes of Heartless that form into Demon Towers, fight apparitions of Ventus and Terra, and save Terra’s heart. Meanwhile, Mickey went to the Realm of Darkness to save Riku. When he meets Aqua after using her lost Wayfinder to find her, he tells her 10 years have passed since they last met and proceeds to Destiny Islands after fighting another Demon Tower. There, the door to Kingdom Hearts is spotted, and Mickey helps Sora and Riku seal it shut, leaving Aqua to dwell in the Realm of Darkness once more.

In the very first entry of the series, Sora sets out on a journey with Donald and Goofy to reunite with Riku and Kairi after the Heartless destroy Destiny Islands and plunge the world into darkness. Along the way, he travels to different worlds aboard the Gummi Ship, meets various Disney and Final Fantasy characters, and helps defend their world from the Heartless by sealing Keyholes. Meanwhile, Maleficent leads a group of her fellow Disney villains to seek out the seven Princesses of Heart to unlock the last keyhole leading to Kingdom Hearts, and she employs Riku.

By the time Sora reaches Hollow Bastion, Kairi’s body is found with her heart missing as it was transferred to Sora’s body during the apocalypse at Destiny Islands; Riku becomes possessed by Ansem, who was manipulating Maleficent to open Kingdom Hearts; and Kairi is revealed to be the Princess of Heart, hence the heart transfer from her to Sora, who then frees Kairi’s heart after impaling himself with Ansem’s Keyblade, turning into a Heartless in the process. Kairi manages to turn Sora back to human form by recognizing his Heartless and embracing him, and from there Sora defeats Ansem and seals the door to Kingdom Hearts with help from Riku and Mickey from the other side.

While searching for Riku and Mickey after sealing the door to Kingdom Hearts, Sora, Donald, and Goofy visit Castle Oblivion, causing them to lose their memories upon entry. They’re told by Marluxia, the lord of the castle who is revealed to be a member of Organization XIII, that the deeper they go into the castle, the more memories they’ll lose, but they'll uncover new ones in the process. The group is given a deck of cards called “world cards” based on Sora’s memories, and they meet memory versions of the characters they met in the previous game and fight a few members of the Organization aside from Marluxia — Axel, Larxene, and Vexen — as they progress through each floor of the castle. Meanwhile, Riku is going through the basement levels of the castle, wrestling with the darkness inside him and Ansem’s attempts to control him while fighting two other members of Organization XIII: Lexaeus and Zexion.

Aside from the cards being decried as an ineffective battle system, Chain of Memories introduced new characters that became essential players in the Kingdom Hearts series, such as Naminé, whom Sora gradually remembered as being an old friend only to find out later she was manipulating Sora’s memories of Kairi by replacing them with fake ones of herself under Marluxia’s orders. After Sora fights Marluxia for his life and Naminé’s freedom, Naminé places him and his companions to sleep in pod-like machines to help them regain the memories they lost.

358/2 Days is set during the events of Chain of Memories. It explores the birth of Roxas as Sora’s Nobody when Sora turned into a Heartless during Kingdom Hearts, his daily life as the 13th member of Organization XIII, and his friendship with Axel and Xion, who mysteriously arrived as the 14th member.

As time progresses and their bond deepens, it is revealed that Xion is an artificial replica created after Sora’s memories of Kairi as a fail-safe if Sora and Roxas are proven to be useless for the Organization to achieve their goal of summoning Kingdom Hearts and becoming whole, all the while delaying Sora’s memory restoration process by absorbing them. This discovery causes Roxas to defect from Organization XIII to find himself, and later Xion, who fights to merge with him to become whole, stopping Sora from waking up. Ultimately, Roxas defeats Xion, who disintegrates into light with all the memories she absorbed returning to Sora.

Fun fact, but not precisely fun: 358/2 was dedicated to the memory of Wayne Allwine, the voice actor for Mickey Mouse, who died 12 days before the game’s release in Japan in May 2009.

The game begins in Twilight Town, where Roxas enjoys his summer vacation with Hayner, Pence, and Olette, having no memories of his time with Organization XIII nor Axel, who remembers him during their encounters while waking up with dreams of Sora, who had been asleep for a year at that point. Once Sora wakes up along with Donald and Goofy after Roxas merges with him, they set out to once again protect the worlds from the Heartless and visit new ones to stop Organization XIII from creating another Kingdom Hearts that would give the Nobodies their hearts back.

As Sora and the gang explore the concept of the heart even further, they learn that the Ansem they fought was Xehanort’s Heartless; Xemnas, the leader of Organization XIII, is Xehanort’s Nobody; and that Xehanort was an apprentice of the real Ansem, named Ansem the Wise, the sage-king of Radiant Garden (renamed Hollow Bastion and then Radiant Garden again) who studied the heart alongside Braig, Dilan, Even, Aeleus, Ienzo (human versions of Xigbar, Xaldin, Vexen, Lexaeus, and Zexion, respectively) to protect his people from darkness before he was exiled to the Realm of Darkness for corrupting them with the same darkness and taking on the new identity DiZ (Darkness in Zero). Even more shocking, they learn Roxas and Naminé are the Nobodies of Sora and Kairi, respectively.

Initially released as an episodic mobile game called “Coded” in Japan, Re:coded centers on King Mickey and a digital version of Sora as they work to repair Jiminy Cricket’s journal, which chronicles the real Sora’s adventures fighting the Heartless and Organization XIII, after it got corrupted. It was being digitized to analyze a secret message Jiminy did not write: “Their hurting will be mended when you return to end it” (originally written as “We must return to free them from their torment” in Coded). In the dataspace, Data-Sora and Mickey fight the bugs, who take the form of red-and-black blocks and Heartless, and work to decipher the message's meaning.

Square Enix originally released eight parts of Coded and a preview to Japanese mobile users from June 2009 to January 2010, making it run almost like a full season of a television series. To make the game accessible to fans worldwide, the entire game was repackaged into Re:coded for the Nintendo DS .

To prepare for Master Xehanort’s return, Master Yen Sid proctors the Mark of Mastery exam to Sora and Riku in the most unconventional way possible: sending them back in time to unlock the keyholes of seven worlds that were left in a sleeping state after being destroyed by the Heartless, including the worlds of Hunchback of Notre Dame, Pinocchio, Tron: Legacy, and Fantasia. Though they go through a different chain of events in the same worlds, they work to defeat the “Nightmare” Dream Eaters with the help of their “Spirit” Dream Eaters and the power of Flowmotion.

Throughout the Mark of Mastery exam, they run into the younger version of Xehanort, who reveals that he, Ansem, and Xehanort, who were supposed to have been defeated, lured Sora into a trap at The World That Never Was and put him into a deep sleep (where he was protected by Ventus’ armor), and Riku has been running through Sora’s dreams as a Dream Eater the whole time. To save Sora from the darkness, Riku fights the young Xehanort, and the revived, older Master Xehanort arrives with intentions to turn Sora into his 13th vessel for the new Organization XIII, comprised of mostly his past selves from across time, and create the χ-blade by pitting the 13 seekers of darkness and the seven guardians of light against each other. Thankfully, Xehanort’s plans are foiled by King Mickey, Lea (the human version of Axel), and Riku, who ultimately passes the Mark of Mastery exam, with Sora failing for losing the power of waking, which is the ability to restore hearts.

In the final chapter of the Dark Seeker Saga, Sora sets out to reclaim the power of waking and gather the seven guardians of light to prepare for the final showdown with Organization XIII and Master Xehanort, who is hellbent on not only creating the χ-blade, but also keeping darkness and light in proper balance. Meanwhile, Kairi trains to become a Keyblade wielder with Lea, and Riku goes with King Mickey to search for the missing Keyblade wielders.

Kingdom Hearts 3 took 13 years to make, with a few trailers released between 2013 and 2018 before finally being released in 2019. To this day, it remains the best-selling Kingdom Hearts game.

Melody of Memory is a rhythm game where Sora and the other Keyblade wielders defeat the Heartless, Nobodies, Unversed, and Dream Eaters to the beat of every song in the series. It’s set against the backdrop of Kairi being in the lab at Radiant Garden, as she gives a summary of the series’ events as the narrator.

Kingdom Hearts 4 was announced in 2022, though Square Enix has been pretty quiet about KH4 since its announcement and has yet to reveal a release window. A series of screenshots were dropped seemingly out of nowhere in mid-2025, and during a Nintendo Direct in June 2026 , the studio revealed a new trailer that does appear to show some gameplay . The trailer also confirmed the game will be playable on the Switch 2 "at launch," whenever that ends up being.

Cristina Alexander is a freelance writer for IGN. She has contributed her work to various publications, including Digital Trends, TheGamer, Twinfinite, Mega Visions, and The Escapist. To paraphrase Calvin Harris, she wears her love for Sonic the Hedgehog on her sleeve like a big deal. Follow her on Twitter @SonicPrincess15.

articles.title: Every Pokémon Game on the Nintendo Switch and Switch 2 in 2026
articles.summary: Gotta play 'em all.
articles.body:
Often cited as one of the world's most valuable media franchises, Pokémon is a household name that's been a Nintendo staple since the Game Boy. The beloved series is home to hundreds of amazing creatures you can catch in-game or collect as trading cards , with each new generation bringing loads more to discover. Every console released by Nintendo has had plenty of Pokémon games released for it, and the Nintendo Switch is no exception.

Pokémon Day brought tons of new announcements about what's next for the franchise. Below, we've compiled every Pokémon game that has been released on Nintendo Switch and the information we have on a number of upcoming Pokémon games releasing on the Switch 2.

How Many Pokémon Games Are There on Nintendo Switch?

In total, 16 Pokémon games have been released for the Nintendo Switch . This includes the mainline games for the 8th and 9th Pokémon generations as well as plenty of spinoffs. For the sake of this list, we've counted mainline entries with two versions as a single release. We also don't include the Pokémon games offered through Nintendo Switch Online , but you can check out that list below.

All Pokémon Games on Nintendo Switch (in Release Order)

Pokkén Tournament was originally released for the Wii U in 2016. A year later, Nintendo and Bandai Namco prepared a deluxe version of the game for Nintendo Switch, adding new characters and updated visuals to take advantage of better hardware. This three-on-three battle system is a blast to play with friends both in person and online.

Pokémon Quest turns all your favorite Pokémon into miniature cube form. This free-to-play Switch game features a fun and simple combat system where you send Pokémon on expeditions. Equip different abilities to your Pokémon to handle all types of encounters.

Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! & Let's Go, Eevee! (2018)

Pokémon: Let's Go, Pikachu! & Pokémon: Let's Go, Eevee! are remakes of the beloved 1998 Pokémon Yellow . These titles were the first mainline Pokémon games ever to release on a home console, since none made it to the Wii U. Set in the Kanto region, all 151 original Pokémon appear with varying forms from previous mainline installments. With heavy accessibility features, these remakes were a great first step for the series on Nintendo Switch for newcomers and veterans of the series.

Pokémon Sword & Shield marked the first installment in the series to feature aspects of an open world. Dubbed the Wild Areas, these regions allowed for free traversal and battles with wild Pokémon. Gyms also made a return for the first time since X & Y. Additionally, Sword & Shield introduced the eigth generation of Pokémon, which included Dynamax and Gigantamax forms of previous Pokémon.

Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Rescue Team DX (2020)

Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Rescue Team DX is a remake of the 2005 titles Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Red Rescue Team & Blue Rescue Team. Surprisingly, this is the first Pokémon spinoff remake ever, with development handled by Spike Chunsoft. The gameplay consists of completing jobs in different dungeons and unlocking new Pokémon along the way.

Pokémon Mystery Dungeon: Rescue Team DX - Nintendo Switch

The other Pokémon release of 2020 was Pokémon Café ReMix featuring similar gameplay to other puzzle games like Disney Tsum Tsum, which requires you to connect Pokémon together to solve puzzles. In Pokémon Café ReMix, you and Eevee own a café and must serve the Pokémon who come for food or a little drink. This charming service game is free-to-play via the Nintendo eShop.

After more than 20 years, the Nintendo Switch is the console that finally received a sequel to Pokémon Snap . Developed by Bandai Namco, you traverse around different biomes and areas with an on-rails camera to capture pictures Pokémon in the wild. You can unlock new courses by taking good pictures in New Pokémon Snap , leaving for a sizeable amount of content to unlock and discover. You never know what you might find during each session!

This free-to-play game marked Pokémon's first entry into the MOBA genre. You command and control a team of five Pokémon in head-to-head battles against other players online. There's a solid amount of Pokémon to choose from, so you can adjust your team to best fit your needs. Pokémon Unite went on to be featured in different esports tournaments, with multiple championships held for the game.

Pokémon Brilliant Diamond & Shining Pearl (2021)

Pokémon Brilliant Diamond & Pokémon Shining Pear l are remakes of Pokémon Diamond & Pearl, which originally released in 2006 for the Nintendo DS . As the fourth generation of Pokémon, Diamond & Pearl feature a wide variety of Pokémon to battle against and discover. The remakes feature a new chibi art style that was created to stay faithful to the original titles while still remaining fresh.

Pokémon Brilliant Diamond & Pokémon Shining Pearl Double Pack - Nintendo Switch

Pokémon Legends: Arceus is often praised as one of the best Pokémon games available on the Switch. This original title takes place far in the past, somewhere in the Hisui region. With a focus on exploration, you can freely walk all around the map to capture Pokémon, explore different environments, and so much more. Pokémon can be spotted wandering around all over the map, which requires you to be strategic if you're looking to avoid battle.

Out Now Pokemon Legends: Arceus for Switch

The latest mainline Pokémon games officially kicked off Generation 9, bringing along an entire new approach to gameplay and world design. In Pokémon Scarlet & Violet , an open world awaits with freedom to explore wherever your heart takes you. The DLC pass, titled The Hidden Treasure of Area Zero, is now wrapped up, making it a perfect time to check out Scarlet & Violet.

Pokémon Scarlet & Violet - Nintendo Switch

One game and one movie later, the sequel to Detective Pikachu is finally available on Nintendo Switch. Tim's father is missing, and it's up to Detective Pikachu to solve the case! This sequel features new puzzles and investigations, where you can investigate scenes and use your notebook to get to the bottom of the mystery. If you're a fan of both Pokémon and mystery games, this is a great game to consider.

Detective Pikachu Returns - Nintendo Switch

Pokémon Legends: Z-A is the most recent release in the series, launching on both Switch systems on October 16. Rebekah Valentine's review for IGN marks a significant shift from the downfalls of the previous generation, describing that "what elevates Lumiose City far above the much larger overworld of Scarlet and Violet is that it’s dense with interesting landmarks, items, obstacle courses, stores, Wild Zones, shops, and people."

The game takes place in the French-inspired Lumiose City, with familiar starters in Tepig, Chikorita, and Totodile, all of which get new Mega Evolutions . A big change in this game is the combat system, which introduces more real-time action .

This is where timelines can be a bit confusing. Pokemon FireRed and LeafGreen are technically remakes of Pokemon Red and Blue that released for the Game Boy Advance in 2004. In 2026, the remakes were released once again for Switch platforms, making this one of the best ways for Switch users to dive into the glory of Gen 1 and the Kanto region .

While we may not be getting a new Animal Crossing game (yet), Nintendo released a new Pokémon spin-off game that should definitely scratch any cozy gaming itch. Pokémon Pokopia makes you a Ditto with a human appearance, who must work and learn from local Pokémon to build new habitats across a massive spread of areas. Build homes for your Pokemon, decorate new areas, and help figure out why all of the humans disappeared. You can learn more about this one, which happens to currently be the highest rated Pokemon game of all time, in our 9/10 review .

The most recent release from Game Freak and The Pokémon Company is Pokémon Champions, a new free-to-play battle game in the spirit of Pokemon Showdown. You can battle with Pokémon you've trained in other games through the Pokémon Home app , but there are some interesting limitations to what Pocket Monsters made the roster cut. Champions will also be the new standard for Play! Pokémon VGC events .

Available Pokémon Games With Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack

The Nintendo Switch Online subscription service has even more options if you're looking for more. Here are the Pokémon games you can play with a Nintendo Switch Online + Expansion Pack membership :

Pokémon Trading Card Game (GameBoy Color)

Pokémon Mystery Dungeon - Red Rescue Team (GameBoy Advance)

Upcoming Pokémon Games on Nintendo Switch

While there may have been some leaks ahead of time, The Pokémon Company officially confirmed the existence of the next mainline Pokémon games, Winds and Waves , on Pokémon Day 2026 . Our first teaser certainly seems to indicate a long-hoped for graphical update, and went right on ahead to reveal the Gen 10 starters : Pombon, Gecqua, and Browt.

The teaser also clarified that the next mainline Pokémon games will be releasing for Switch 2 in 2027, marking a full five years since Gen 9.

Noah Hunter is a freelance writer and reviewer with a passion for games and technology. He co-founded Final Weapon, an outlet focused on nonsense-free Japanese gaming (in 2019) and has contributed to various publishers writing about the medium.

Magic: The Gathering's next Marvel crossover set has been revealed , as Wizards of the Coast announced that "Marvel: Darkhold Destiny" will launch on April 9, 2027.

Preorders are now available via local game stores, TCGplayer , Amazon , and other retailers. I'll leave links to where you can buy everything just below.

"The world's greatest sorcerers conspired to keep the Darkhold sealed," Wizards of the Coast (WOTC) said in its announcement, as part of New York Comic Con. "But the dark side of the Marvel Universe has been unleashed!"

It also teased the arrival of "devils, sorcerers, and vampire-hunting vampires" in the upcoming set, which will of course explore the supernatural side of Marvel.

An original story has been developed for the new set, with WOTC developing in collaboration with Marvel, which will also introduce a brand-new original character. The story will also be adapted into a special Marvel Comics release, written by Jackson Lanzing and Collin Kelly.

Magic: The Gathering – Marvel Darkhold Destiny New Cards

"This story was crafted by our Narrative team with Magic in mind, and we're thrilled to see it adapted by two of Marvel's most beloved writers," added WOTC.

"You'll be able to follow this dimension-hopping narrative across the set, all while uncovering the secrets of the Dark Dimension and joining forces with Marvel's pantheon of gods."

The comic is due to arrive in February 2027 in digital format, followed by a physical release in April.

Magik, a mutant sorceress who many fans will also recognize from Marvel Rivals ' roster, or more recently Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls , is the only hero confirmed for the set so far.

But WOTC has also said that the expansion will feature plenty more "hotly anticipated" Marvel heroes and villains making their MTG debuts.

Magic: The Gathering – Marvel Darkhold Destiny Art

Marvel: Darkhold Destiny will include the main card set, Commander decks, Scene Boxes, and special collector-focused card designs.

The Commander precon options this time around are Lords of Hel (red-black), Gods of Asgard (red-green-white), Strange Academy (white-blue-black) and Midnight Sons (white-black).

WOTC says it has also developed new "Booster Fun treatments" for the expansion, alongside updated versions of designs used in previous releases, "so collectors of everything Marvel will have plenty to get excited for".

Darkhold Destiny is one of the latest collaborations between Marvel and Magic: The Gathering, which has been increasingly drawing established entertainment franchises to the TCG through its Universes Beyond range.

In 2025, we saw the Marvel Spider-Man set , and in 2026, we got the Marvel Super Heroes expansion as well.

Now in 2027, Darkhold Destiny continues the longstanding collaboration between the entertainment giants.

Robert Anderson is a Senior Commerce Editor for IGN. Based in London, UK, he is a qualified journalist with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism (First Class Degree) and over seven years of professional writing and editing experience.

You can usually find Robert lost in open-world RPG games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077. Outside of gaming, his passions include reading comics (especially Superman, Batman, and Spider-Man), taking photos, and keeping up with the latest in film and TV.

His primary coverage focuses on tracking down the best gaming deals and diving into the fast-paced world of Trading Card Games (TCGs). He regularly covers everything from the latest releases in Pokémon TCG and the most expensive cards to comprehensive Magic: The Gathering buying guides .

articles.title: Will Smith is in a slump, but benching him isn't an option for Dodgers
articles.summary: Will Smith's vital contributions at catcher mean the Dodgers can't afford to bench him even though he has struggled mightily at the plate this postseason.
articles.body:
The Dodgers have a big hole in the middle of their batting order, and it's not Shohei Ohtani .

If anything, Ohtani has reemerged as an offensive force in the cleanup spot, singling, walking and scoring the Dodgers' only run Sunday in a 2-1 loss to the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 1 of the National League Championship Series .

The problem is with the guy hitting in front of Ohtani.

Will Smith walked in four plate appearances, marking just the second time he's reached base in the postseason. In the four division series games against the Atlanta Braves, he had a single in 16 at-bats, striking out seven times. He's hitting .053 in the playoffs — only Cleveland's Ángel Martínez has a lower average among players with at least nine at-bats.

But there's not much the Dodgers can do about it. They are built to win with pitching and Smith, the catcher, is the guy they rely on to guide those pitchers through games.

Dalton Rushing , who started just three fewer games behind the plate than Smith this season, is injured and not on the roster. Hunter Feduccia , who did make the team, caught just 15 complete games this season and isn't an option to start in the playoffs.

"I'm not going to put Feduccia in place of Will Smith," Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. "That's just not going to happen."

So Roberts and the Dodgers are left to muddle on with Smith regardless of how much he struggles offensively. That's because he's far more valuable crouching behind the plate than standing next to it.

"I don't even know how he's performing offensively," said Tarik Skubal , who took the loss Sunday. "Catchers, I think it's the most important position on the field. They're the ones calling pitches, dictating game flow, rhythm, all that type of stuff. I'm going to trust those guys always."

Smith appears to be executing his catching duties very well, since opponents have scored just 10 runs and are hitting .160 against the Dodgers this postseason. Only Tampa Bay, which has played two fewer games, has done better.

As for what Smith thinks, that's unknown because the Dodgers did not make him available to the media Sunday. But since he's not coming out of the lineup, the next-best solution might be moving him to another spot in the order.

That worked with Ohtani, who had as many strikeouts as hits in the first two games of the division series, when he batted second. Since being dropped in the order, he has reached base four times in three games, stolen a base and scored twice.

"There's always lineup construction. I can think it through. He's not swinging the bat well," Roberts said of Smith. "It's hard because of the body of work, he just has that knack to get a hit, to get a big hit."

That's exactly what happened last fall when Smith's two-out, 11th-inning home run in Game 7 of the World Series helped the Dodgers win a second straight title .

Smith was on the injured list for 86 days this summer because of neck disk inflammation, returning for the final month when he slashed .290/.400/.548. He has cooled off considerably in October, just as he did last year, when he returned from a right hand contusion three games into the playoffs and got just two hits in his first 14 at-bats.

He recovered to bat .400 in last year's NLCS win over Milwaukee, then broke a 4-4 tie with his winning homer against the Toronto Blue Jays. Just as important, though, Smith caught all but 11 innings in the Dodgers' final 15 postseason games — including two 11-inning games and another that lasted 18 innings.

Smith rarely has hit well in the postseason, batting just .206 in 18 series, which may explain Roberts' lack of panic. Plus, Roberts knows his All-Star catcher has helped him win three World Series rings, and if the Dodgers are to get another, it will be on the strength of their pitching, not their hitting.

And that side of Smith's game is as strong as ever.

"To be honest, that's not where my focus is with Will," Skubal said of his catcher's hitting. "My focus is what he's doing behind the dish and he's very important. He's very important to the entire pitching staff."

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Dodgers drop Game 1 of NLCS in Milwaukee
articles.summary: The Dodgers had their chances. They had runners in scoring position, chased Jacob Misiorowski from the mound before he could complete five innings, and recei...
articles.body:
MILWAUKEE — The Dodgers had their chances. They had runners in scoring position, chased Jacob Misiorowski from the mound before he could complete five innings, and received three scoreless innings from their bullpen. But when the Dodgers needed one final swing to change the outcome, Mookie Betts came up short.

The Dodgers dropped Game 1 of the National League Championship Series on Sunday, falling 2-1 to the Milwaukee Brewers at American Family Field. The Dodgers now trail 0-1 in the series, and Milwaukee has already accomplished something it couldn't do last postseason: take the opening game and put itself in position to avoid another sweep at the hands of the Dodgers.

With Game 1 decided by a single run, the Dodgers were left to wonder what might have been after repeatedly failing to capitalize on their scoring opportunities.

The final chance came in the ninth inning.

After pinch hitter Josue De Paula worked a walk to put runners on first and second, the Dodgers brought the potential tying run into scoring position. Betts, who led off for the Dodgers with Shohei Ohtani batting fourth, stepped to the plate with an opportunity to extend the game.

Instead, Betts lifted a deep fly ball to center field, ending the game and sending Milwaukee into celebration.

For a Dodgers team accustomed to playing deep into October, the loss was a frustrating start to a series that figures to test both clubs.

"It's going to be a long series. We knew it coming in," Dave Roberts said.

Roberts reiterated that sentiment when discussing Milwaukee's position as the team with the best regular-season record in baseball.

"You can't go into a long series against a team that has the best record in baseball and expect to just win 4. It's going to be a long series, we knew it coming in," Roberts said.

The Dodgers' offense never found the consistent rhythm needed to overcome Milwaukee's pitching.

The Dodgers managed five hits against Misiorowski, who worked 4⅓ innings and allowed one run while striking out five and walking three. The Dodgers eventually forced the Brewers to turn to their bullpen, but the damage never materialized into a comeback.

Andy Pages accounted for the Dodgers' lone run with a second-inning RBI single. Beyond that, the Dodgers struggled to turn baserunners into runs, leaving several opportunities unfinished.

One of the most significant moments came in the sixth inning, when the Dodgers had runners on the corners against Abner Uribe. With a chance to tie the game or take the lead, Pages struck out to end the threat.

That failure loomed large as Milwaukee's bullpen continued to shut down the Dodgers.

The ninth inning offered one final opportunity, but Betts' flyout ensured the Dodgers would leave Milwaukee without a win to open the series.

Skubal Keeps Dodgers in the Fight, but Brewers Take Control

The pitching matchup between Tarik Skubal and Misiorowski delivered the kind of tense October baseball expected from two teams with championship aspirations.

Skubal struck out seven over five innings, allowing five hits, two walks and two earned runs on 81 pitches. Although he escaped a bases-loaded jam in the fifth, Milwaukee eventually found the breakthrough it needed.

Garrett Mitchell opened the inning with a walk before Cooper Pratt moved him into scoring position with a bunt. Luis Lara followed with an RBI single, bringing Mitchell home to give the Brewers a 2-1 advantage.

Roberts turned to Alex Vesia for the left-handed portion of Milwaukee's lineup after Skubal completed his outing. The Dodgers' bullpen delivered three scoreless innings, keeping the deficit at one run and giving the offense an opportunity to respond.

It was a strong relief effort, but the Dodgers couldn't provide the tying run.

Despite the disappointment, the Dodgers were quick to emphasize that one loss does not define a seven-game series.

Freddie Freeman acknowledged the frustration while keeping the team's focus on the bigger picture.

"Any loss in the playoffs is not great, but it's a long series. It's just the first game," Freeman said.

Freeman also expressed confidence heading into Monday, with Yoshinobu Yamamoto scheduled to take the ball for Game 2.

"It's just the first game. We'll come back out tomorrow with Yamamoto, I feel pretty confident," Freeman said.

Betts delivered a similar message following his game-ending flyout.

"We got to focus on the task at hand, and that's winning the game tomorrow," Betts said.

For a Dodgers club that entered the postseason with championship expectations, the challenge now is to turn that confidence into a response on the field.

One of the Dodgers' other concerns entering Game 2 is the production of Will Smith.

Smith went 0-for-3 in the opener and has yet to look like his usual self since returning from the injured list. His continued struggles have raised questions about whether the Dodgers might consider giving Hunter Feduccia an opportunity behind the plate.

Roberts, however, made his position clear.

"I'm not going to put Feduccia in place of Will Smith," Roberts said.

The Dodgers are sticking with their veteran catcher, trusting that his experience and offensive ability will eventually translate into better results.

With the series just beginning, Roberts appears unwilling to make a drastic lineup change based on one game.

Yamamoto Gets the Ball With the Series on the Line

The Dodgers won't have much time to dwell on Sunday's defeat. Game 2 arrives Monday afternoon, with Yamamoto tasked with helping the Dodgers avoid falling into an 0-2 hole before the series shifts back to Los Angeles.

Roberts made it clear that he remains confident in his starter.

"They got Henderson, we got Yamamoto. We feel good with our guy," Roberts said.

He reinforced that belief when discussing the urgency of the next game.

"We've got our guy going tomorrow, who we trust undoubtedly. We need to win a baseball game."

The message was straightforward: the Dodgers don't need to solve the entire series on Monday. They need to even it.

Milwaukee, meanwhile, has already secured the result it wanted. After being swept by the Dodgers in last year's postseason meeting, the Brewers have struck first and put the pressure on the defending champions.

The Dodgers still have plenty of baseball ahead of them, but Sunday's loss exposed the importance of converting scoring opportunities when the margins are this thin.

A second-inning RBI single from Pages wasn't enough. Three scoreless innings from the bullpen weren't enough. And a late rally that put the tying run within reach ultimately ended with Betts' fly ball to end of the game.

Yamamoto takes the mound Monday, and the Dodgers will look to leave American Family Field with the series tied before heading back to Dodger Stadium for Game 3 on Wednesday.

As Roberts made clear after Game 1, this series was never expected to be easy.

The Dodgers have their first setback. Their response will determine how much it matters.

articles.title: Riftbound: Radiance Hands-On Preview and Interview - Riftbound Embraces Complexity
articles.summary: I played Riftbound fifth set, Radiance, in Pre-Rift and sealed formats and spoke with executive producer Chengran Chai, who spoke on how Deploy is primed to disrupt the meta and more.
articles.body:
Riftbound’s final set of the year, Radiance , is finally upon us, and I went hands-on with the cards at a very early Pre-Rift tournament. This marks the League of Legends TCG’s fifth set, and features musically-inspired designs and brand new mechanics poised to disrupt the meta.

I also had the chance to talk with Chengran Chai, the executive producer of Riftbound, to get some insight about the set straight from the source in a joint interview with Temple of Geek’s Myles Obenza.

First, a quick recap of the new mechanics being introduced in Radiance, with some of Chai’s commentary:

New Radiance Keywords: Disarm, Show Off, Deploy

Disarm is the simplest of the new mechanics: When your unit with Disarm attacks , it reduces the might of an enemy unit at that battlefield, usually by one. It immediately made me think of Ahri’s original abilities, which is fitting, since the new green (Calm) Ahri, Confident, comes with Disarm. Her unit has a built-in buff when you reduce the Might of an enemy unit, gaining +1 Might herself. The promising new blue (Mind) Kai’sa, Rebel, has both Disarm and gives spells Reaction speed when in a showdown.

Show Off is a mechanic that might be familiar to you if you’ve played other popular TCGs. Cards with Show Off gain an additional effect if you “Show Off” a qualifying card to your opponent as you play it. We’ve only seen four cards in Radiance with Show Off so far–two units and two spells–and they each grant totally different effects. The 5-cost yellow (Order) Spell Rousing Display (clearly part of the Legend Seraphine’s kit) plays four 1-Might Recruit Tokens to your base instead of just one if you Show Off a card with Energy cost 7 or more.

Chai said that Show Off is a trade off–you’re giving away information in exchange for something, but TCGs are very much a game of information. “If I’m planning a spell heavy deck, whether you have Defy or not in your hand matters a great deal to me,” Chai explained. “Show Off basically opens up another dimension to the kind of like, 3D, 4D chess–that’s 5D.” Maybe you show your opponent something you have on purpose to throw them off, pushing them into a play you have the perfect counter-play for. Show Off has the possibility of granting great effects, but it opens the game up for more mind games, too.

Deploy is a keyword specifically for Gear, allowing you to deploy that Gear straight to a Battlefield. While there, it’ll provide an effect, but will be killed if your opponent holds the Battlefield it’s at.

“I think Deploy is probably the one that will disrupt [the meta], because historically, you don't think of just going straight to a battlefield,” Chai said. “And now you have, like, Jarvan IV’s E-Q, you have Ziggs just tossing bombs onto battlefields, and it's going to change the way people think about Defending quite a bit.” Jarvan IV’s “E-Q” that Chai references is the move combo in League of Legends where he throws his flag and then pulls himself there–pretty 1-to-1 with Jarvan IV’s Legend ability in Riftbound, which lets you move a friendly unit to a Battlefield when you play a Gear with Deploy there (and pay 1 Power).

Orianna's Legend ability allows you to turn a friendly Gear into a Gear Unit at the start of your Main Phase, a pretty tricky and cool thing you can do to steal some points with Deployable Gear! Her Signature Gear, The Ball, is especially interesting as it also gains Ganking, allowing it to roll back and forth between battlefields each turn. Chai seemed to be especially high on Orianna along with Deploy, noting her Legend and The Ball as playable cards he'd want to showcase from this set.

Both Show Off and Deploy up the complexity of Riftbound. But, Deploy and Disarm seem to be mechanics that will absolutely disrupt defensive Hold strategies the most, which is especially scary for me as someone who’s playing Akali and Vex with Astral Heron hold strategies!

Last time I got to play with a set early, it was strictly with a preconstructed showcase deck behind closed doors, and I didn’t have more than thirty minutes to actually play with the cards. This time, however, we got a Pre-Rift tournament plus packs to take home to tinker with. So, I played Radiance with one seeded Pre-Rift deck and built two “Sealed” decks to test out–some of which were more successful than others!

In my Radiance Pre-Rift Kit, I got the orange (Body) and yellow (Order) Jarvan IV, Exemplar of Demacia Legend. Jarvan’s Legend ability makes use of the new Deploy keyword: “When you play a gear with [Deploy], you may exhaust me and pay [1 Power] to move a friendly unit to that battlefield.”

I threw in plenty of Gears with Deploy, cards with Gear synergies, plus a couple purple (Chaos) cards that made Bombs, drew cards, and generated Gold so I’d have a decent supply of Power to activate Jarvan IV’s Legend Ability. I removed the 7-cost Jarvan IV, Royal Heir as my chosen Champion Unit, though, and replaced it with the K’Sante, Courageous I pulled. High-cost chosen champions aren’t generally the best move, especially in the speedy Pre-Rift format, and though K’sante still costs a pretty hefty 5 runes, having a Unit with Accelerate at my fingertips in the late game proved to be invaluable.

I can’t say I was thrilled at opening Jarvan IV at first (I was hoping for Riven or Evelynn), but after playing just a few turns, the deck strategy clicked spectacularly for me. I was also lucky enough to get a new battlefield called Hunter’s Circle, which reads, “For each player, the first unit or gear they play here on their turn costs 1 less,” which goes super well with Deployable Gear, since you can play them to the battlefield whenever you want on your turn!

In my first game, a test match, I went second. I played Concert Poster to Hunter’s Circle for free, allowing me to then play Skystrike Squadron for a reduced cost of 3 for returning Concert Poster to my hand. A 4-Might Unit with Reflect on my first turn: Not bad! On my next turn, I was able to create two Recruits with Concert Poster and Buff a Recruit and my Skystrike Squadron with Pillaged Armory. Maybe some godlike luck allowed for this to happen, but it felt pretty dang nifty!

With this build, I have to shoutout Portable Portal, a 2-cost orange (Body) Gear with Deploy. When I showed this card to someone, they said they knew it’d be a menace just because Teemo is on it. When you play it, you can pay one orange (Body) power to ready a Unit. Friendly units at that battlefield with Portable Portal also have Ganking. These abilities paired with the Jarvan IV Legend allowed for double conquering in one turn, or allowing for a Gank and then a retreat with Jarvan’s ability, protecting my Unit. It’s a rare card, though, so pulling it in a Pre-Rift isn’t exactly guaranteed!

In my two Sealed games, one of the decks had no discernible theme besides trying to make Seraphine work (I did not). In the other, I tried for a Ziggs / Bomb build because I happened to pull his Legend and his Epic-rarity red (Fury) Unit, Ziggs, Short-Fused. Let me tell you, the Bomb strategy is pretty tricky to hold together if you don’t have a very reliable way to detonate them on your opponent’s turn. Usually, they explode, dealing two damage per bomb when your opponent holds the battlefield they’re deployed at.

I found it fairly difficult to get enough bombs on a battlefield to matter in one turn unless I held with Explosimian, which lets you play three Bomb gear tokens to a single battlefield. Of course, this still does nothing for protecting you if you’re trying to hold your bomb-ridden battlefield. However, the Pre-Rift Seeded decks with the Ziggs Legend includes the 4-might purple (Chaos) Champion Unit Ziggs, Explosive, which allows you to kill a friendly gear when he defends! If you have enough Bombs, you could potentially wipe your opponent before they can even touch you. And if they can, well, Ziggs, Explosive gets +2 Might if he killed a friendly gear that turn!

Unfortunately, I did not have this Ziggs Unit in my Sealed game, so a different strategy was in order. We determined it’s likely best to load Bombs up one battlefield, leave them alone, and then build a strong Hold at the other Battlefield, forcing your opponent to choose to deal with either a battlefield fortified with Units or fortified with Bombs.

The Unit Reckless Innovator and Gear The Good Stuff, both The purple (Chaos) cards, also proved to be very useful in just about every thrown together deck I or my opponent played. I have a lot more opinions, but it’d be absurd to expect you to read my ramblings, so we’ll end it at that.

Overall, the Sealed and Pre-Rift formats for Radiance were very fun, and the new ideas this set brings to Riftbound add an even higher level of complexity to the existing pool. As for Radiance in a vacuum for Sealed, it seemed to allow for a good variety of unique deck-building options. This is of course by design.

“We want the base set to have a rich enough playing set,” Chai said. “Such that Sealed events are fun… all by itself.”

Riftbound: Radiance - Music ONs, SPs, and Alt Runes

With the playing set determined, that’s when the Riftbound team layers collectibility on top of it with Alt Art, Overnumbered, and SP cards. Some of the rare standouts for Radiance are Riot Games Music crossovers, including the Overnumbered Heartsteel cards, SP K/DA cards, and Overnumbered Ekko, Revolutionary, which features Ekko’s original True Damage skin. The Overnumbered cards also come in the Signature variety, which are the rarest pulls besides the single Ultimate Rare in this set.

“We knew Riot as a whole would have a music moment towards the end of the year, so very early on, we said we would lean into that,” Chai said. However, as a physical game, the Riftbound team needed to finalize many card details before the songs were even composed and the new character designs were finished. “That is why you see… for the K/DA and Heartsteel cards, it is very much their K/DA All Out and Heartsteel 1.0 versions, because the 2.0 versions just weren’t quite ready,” Chai said. “But we thought it would be a great way to showcase Riftbound’s participation… and leverage the broader music moment to allow more fans to see and experience Riftbound as well.”

This original plan didn’t even include teasing Heartsteel’s Riftbound cards in Heartsteel’s new Live My Life music video–the Riot Music Team actually initiated that easter egg, asking the Riftbound team if they wanted the cards in the music video. Of course, they said yes.

Though Riftbound has been very supported from within Riot since the beginning, the somewhat unexpected explosion of its popularity has given Riftbound even more opportunities to be a part of Riot-wide moments. Another example of this is the Riftbound easter egg in Valorant’s Aeris Flex cosmetic.

The Heartsteel Overnumbered cards feature a very unique design, akin to K-pop photo cards, complete with bright motifs, stickers, and Y2K elements. Playing into the photo card inspiration even more, the Heartsteel Overnumbered Signature cards are "signed" by the characters themselves--not the artists like on other Signature cards! Riot Games’ senior Manager of creative development Michelle Mauk spoke about the design process during the Radiance panel at the Riftbound Regional Qualifier (RQ) in Los Angeles , which I highly recommend you watch if you’re interested.

I always feel like renders of Overnumbered cards don’t do them justice, and that’s certainly the case for the Heartsteel cards, too. The texturing and foiling on Riftbound’s most coveted cards are always so impressive to behold in person.

Radiance’s Ultimate Rare ties well into the heavy music theme but is, shockingly, a Battlefield: Packed Amphitheater. This card will be the rarest card in all of Riftbound’s main sets, only appearing in about 0.025% of booster packs. That’s a huge rarity uptick from the only other Ultimate Rare, Baron Nasher from Unleashed, with a 0.1% pack rate. The in-person foiling and texturing you can't see in a render does a lot a lot of heavy lifting for this one–and you can get a better look at it, and see some creators’ reactions, in this official PlayRiftbound reel.

There are other Overnumbers and Alt Art cards to chase that aren’t musically inclined, too, like the Overnumbererd Mordekaiser Legend IGN exclusively revealed last week .

Radiance Pre-Rifts start at local game stores near you on Oct. 16, and I really can’t wait to play some more. With the complexity Radiance introduces, this might not be the best first set to get into, but it’s great for existing players craving more variety and creativity in their deck building. That being said, the Riftbound community has always been nothing but welcoming and helpful at every store I’ve played at, too, so don’t be shy. Otherwise, Radiance booster boxes, packs, and vaults will be available to purchase on Oct. 23.

Casey DeFreitas is the deputy editor of guides at IGN and is playing three more Riftbound Radiance Pre-Rifts this weekend at a local game store, because they're just that much fun. Catch her on socials @ShinyCaseyD .

articles.title: Latest Leaked GTA 6 Video Shows Lucia Fully Naked, Sparks Fan Skepticism
articles.summary: The GTA 6 leaker has reportedly released yet another unauthorized gameplay video, this time allegedly showing Lucia fully naked in a bid to push their crypto scheme. However, some now suspect Cyberleek is using a developer build or cheats to make Jason and Lucia naked, and that the leaked gameplay does not accurately represent GTA 6 as it will play at launch.
articles.body:
UPDATE: Cyberleek has reportedly followed through on their threat to release a “Lucia closeup 4k” video, and is once again tying further leaks to crypto market cap targets, ranging from $5 million to $25 million. According to online reports, Cyberleek has threatened to release a new unauthroized GTA 6 gameplay video every day, assuming the memecoin market cap targets are met. However, the Cyberleek memecoin has crashed, with a current market cap of $2.5 million.

Fans have spent the last week calling on people not to spend money on Cyberleek, pointing to the person or group's previous form when it came to cashing out in August. With GTA 6 little over a month away, it seems Cyberleek is doubling down on their crypto scheme one last time.

ORIGINAL STORY: The GTA 6 leaker has reportedly released yet another unauthorized gameplay video, this time allegedly showing Lucia fully naked in a bid to push their crypto scheme. However, some now suspect Cyberleek is using a developer build or cheats to make Jason and Lucia naked, and that the leaked gameplay does not accurately represent GTA 6 as it will play at launch.

Cyberleek had threatened to release gameplay showing Lucia fully naked if the market cap of their memecoin hit $4 million. That was achieved over the weekend. However, while the new video reportedly does show Lucia fully naked, there are a number of signs that some believe suggest Cyberleek has tinkered with the build they allegedly have access to .

One suspected telltale sign from the previous leak was that a tank was spawned into the game world, suggesting access to a dev menu of some kind. Now, with two leaked videos allegedly showing both Jason and Lucia fully naked but NPCs in the game world failing to react to that in any way, some believe this effect was achieved with either a dev menu or cheats.

In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023

One theory is that Cyberleak was able to access this state for both Lucia and Jason because in at least one mission players will see both characters naked, perhaps in a nudist resort. As it stands, this is all speculation, and it is unknown if GTA 6 will feature either character naked at any point — officially at least.

Cyberleek has doubled down on their crypto scheme in the last week, threatening Rockstar and parent company Take-Two with the release of a full playthrough of the game’s story if they fail to release GTA 6 on-disc and issue a public apology — and the market cap of their memecoin hits $30 million. Of course, few believe these GTA 6 leaks are about campaigning for physical media — rather they're about making money from cryptocurrency.

To that end, Cyberleek has polled people on the release of a “Lucia closeup 4k video,” which suggests further leaks are incoming.

A cryptocurrency market capitalization (market cap) is the total dollar value of all the coins or tokens of a digital asset currently in circulation. At the time of this article’s publication, Cyberleek had a market cap of $2.7 million, having spiked at $8.4 million on October 11 as people pushed for the release of the latest gameplay. It seems unlikely that it will get anywhere near $30 million.

Cyberleek appeared to go dark after a spate of high-profile GTA 6 leaks in August that sparked an investigation from Rockstar parent company Take-Two. The company issued subpoenas to the likes of Discord as part of the hunt for the person or group of people responsible. But Cyberleek reemerged last week with the release of a 24-minute GTA 6 gameplay video that showed cutscenes, story beats, playable characters Jason and Lucia naked (in the case of Jason, full-frontal nudity), and a first-person camera.

It remains unclear how the gameplay footage, or any potential build of the game it's taken from, escaped the confines of Rockstar's infamous tight security. This week’s developments suggest Cyberleek remains at large and defiant in the face of potential legal action.

In August, Rockstar addressed the GTA 6 leaks , describing the situation as "heartbreaking" for its development team and "unfortunate" for fans. At the time, the developer acknowledged that its intended experience for players "may now be impacted by some spoilers," but reiterated GTA 6's previously-confirmed launch date of November 19.

Analysis of cryptocurrency transactions in late August pointed to the GTA 6 leaker having "cashed out," earning around $270,000 in the process. Every video posted by Cyberleek pointed to a website where fans could pay to vote on further leaks using the leaker's own cryptocurrency. Such a poll is reportedly live on Cyberleek's website now , suggesting yet another leak is on the way.

Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: Gears of War: E-Day Dev Confirms DDoS Attack
articles.summary: Gears of War: E-Day suffered a DDoS attack over the weekend, developer The Coalition has said.
articles.body:
Gears of War: E-Day suffered a DDoS attack over the weekend, developer The Coalition has said.

Players suffered intermittent disconnects and login issues while trying to play the Xbox Series X and S and PC action game, which The Coalition eventually got on top of. It has now confirmed the problems were the result of a distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack targeting online services.

“Our teams are continuing to monitor and mitigate this activity. We’ll provide updates if there are any significant changes,” The Coalition said . “Thank you for your patience and understanding.”

There is a great deal of speculation online about the motivation behind hitting Gears with a DDoS attack, with some pointing to a continued online vendetta against the game for apparently being “woke.” E-Day has a “mostly positive” user review rating on Steam. Whatever the reason (there may be no overarching reason behind the DDoS attack at all), E-Day is now up and running.

Last week, Alinea Analytics' head of marketing analysis, Rhys Elliott, reported that E-Day had sold an estimated 230,000 copies in its first week in what was described as a soft start. These unofficial figures, which are not backed by data provided by Microsoft, pointed to Xbox subscription service Game Pass as cannibalizing sales.

Earlier this month, the boss of The Coalition responded to reports that staff at the studio were worried they might lose their jobs amid the ongoing cuts at Xbox, promising the next Gears game wouldn’t take as long to make.

Eurogamer had reported on internal concern that layoffs would hit The Coalition after the release of E-Day. "The mood is certainly 'let's not celebrate the game until we're three months post launch, just in case,' which is very unusual," one source told the site. "We're just expecting the next wave [of layoffs], or being reorganized under Activision or something later this year," claimed another.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma’s “reset” of Microsoft’s gaming business has seen nearly 2,000 people cut already this financial year, with more to come. A number of studios have left the business or are in the process of closing down. Microsoft has also reorganized its studios, bringing Halo and Sea of Thieves developer Rare under Call of Duty developer Activision, and Grounded developer Obsidian under Fallout developer Bethesda.

Of course, Gears of War: E-Day was selected to be an Xbox Series X and S and PC game, ditching any release for a sales-boosting PS5 version. The Coalition studio head Mike Crump recently told the BBC that success for E-Day goes behind sales, saying: "We measure things like, are we showcasing the platform? Are we pushing the hardware to its limits? Are we showcasing what the Xbox is capable of? ...Our goal basically is to be the best-looking game on the Xbox and really show the industry what's possible with our hardware.”
